what: One mutant per assertion of the combat balance slice, rule 21 and criterion 5 of Issue #336. Every substitution below is the changed fragment of code verbatim, not a description of it.

tree.why: Issue #147 measured the trap: a mutant run on an uncommitted tree is reverted together with the edit it was meant to check. Every run below was taken with the tree clean at ffba85a, and reverted with `git checkout -- src/ tests/` afterwards.

howEachWasRun.baselineOfTheUnmutatedTree: Simulation 359 of 360 passed with one Skip (Issue #380); Presentation 735 of 735; DomainMcp 8 of 8. The one new check of this round, The_same_exchange_gives_a_different_result, brings the simulation total from 359 to 360.

mutants.assertion: criterion 1 of #336 — two runs of one seed give one canonical document byte for byte over a whole party
mutants.substitutionTo: private int CombatJitter(int amplitude) => System.Random.Shared.Next(amplitude * 2 + 1) - amplitude;
mutants.whatItBites: the source of the draw, which is the whole of the hard constraint of #336: the spread may only come from the party's seed
mutants.noteOnTheThirdOne: The pre-existing economy replay reddens too, and it is worth naming why the new check was still needed: it runs to FirstRaidTick + 1 and can only see this substitution through the raider MIGHT jitter, which is drawn from the same stream on raider entry. No blow has landed at that tick, so nothing it asserts is about the damage draw.

mutants.assertion: criterion 3 of #336 — the same exchange gives a different result
mutants.whatItBites: the amplitude itself — with it zeroed a blow is exactly might*W + readiness/D and two blows of one profile can no longer differ

thisMutantChangedTheSliceAndThatIsTheFin.whatHappenedFirst: Run against the check as it was first written, the mutant came back GREEN. The check grouped blows by the profile m{Might}r{Readiness} read off the snapshot taken at the END of the tick, and Readiness is republished there: a defender that struck and was wounded on the same tick publishes the wounded value (injury_light_penalty 15, heavy 40). With the amplitude at zero the plain profile still showed 5..8 «scattered» profiles a party — m1r23 => 7/10, a gap of three where there was no draw at all.
thisMutantChangedTheSliceAndThatIsTheFin.whatWasChanged: The assertion was restricted to blows whose striker published the same might AND the same readiness at both ends of the tick it struck on. In that set no term of might*W + readiness/D + jitter can move except the draw. Commit ffba85a.
thisMutantChangedTheSliceAndThatIsTheFin.afterTheChange: steadyScattered = 0 in all six fighting parties under the mutant, 19..31 without it, on 104..171 steady blows of 127..200. The check reddens.
thisMutantChangedTheSliceAndThatIsTheFin.whyItIsRecorded: Because the six reddened checks above would have been enough to satisfy the letter of criterion 5 while no check said anything about the spread — they speak about the party score, about memory of place and about contract invariants. That is the shape open as Issue #340: a mutant that lands on a consequence and is read as coverage of the claim.

mutants.assertion: readiness / 6 is the coefficient the slice's restored properties rest on
mutants.whatItBites: the resolution with which hunger reaches a blow. At 25 the whole range of readiness is worth four whole numbers of damage, which is the state the slice was raised out of.
mutants.result: RED, 1 of the 2 checks the constant's own note named

greenAndItIsAFinding.measuredAt1000: green — that is, with readiness contributing nothing to a blow at all
greenAndItIsAFinding.consequence: The note beside the constant promised that both checks go red when the divisor is raised. One of them does. The name of the other was removed from the note in this same commit rather than left standing: a note naming a check that cannot fail is read as coverage. Round 3 of this slice removed exactly this kind of false promise from the neighbouring constant and wrote down that it must not be reintroduced; it was, one constant over, and the mutant is what found it.

mutants.assertion: cell occupancy in the pathfinder, the domain's side — Issue #76 as this slice raised it
mutants.whatItBites: the call site, which is exactly the pre-#76 code: the pathfinder stops seeing bodies and a creature walks into one, is refused, and walks into it again next tick

whatStayedGreenAndItIsSaidPlainly.why: This is the check the jam showed up in — one creature, one sixty-tick window, baseline/20260728, `mode=Moving last=waiting_blocked_by_other` — and it is what commit 2b69117 named as the reason #76 was raised out of slice 6. Reverting this one call site on the FINAL party does not reproduce it: the party the jam was measured on had a different threshold, a different damage denomination and a blind raider pathfinder as well. So the jam has no check that reproduces it by this substitution alone, and the observable price of #76 on this party is the memory-of-place family above. Named rather than dressed up: nothing here proves the jam cannot come back, only that memory of place stops being observable without the fix.

mutants.assertion: cell occupancy in the pathfinder, the raiders' side — criterion 1 of Issue #76
mutants.substitutionTo: (the whole block removed, so a raider's blocked set holds the forbidden zone and its own remembered place only — which is what RaiderBlockedTiles was before this slice)
mutants.whatItBites: the raider pathfinder's knowledge of other raiders. The hard step check in RaiderStep is deliberately left in place, so what this measures is the PATHFINDING half of #76 on its own.

mutants.assertion: RaiderBlockedPatience — criterion 2 of Issue #76, a blocked body must not stall silently
mutants.whatItBites: the limit on the wait. With no limit a raider queued behind an occupied tile waits for ever, no wave after the first resolves, and the party runs to SessionTicks with a null outcome.
red: the whole PrototypeReturningRaiderTests family, the memory family, and eleven more — 29 in total
mutants.note: This is the measurement the constant's own comment records, taken again here: the limit is not a nicety, it is what keeps the party finishing.

mutants.assertion: the observability floor of memory of place, in the derived form of commit e8d6519 — memory of place is observable in EVERY party of the matrix
mutants.whatItBites: AvoidedPlace now returns null always, so a memory is written and published but never changes what a creature does — memory not observed AT ALL, which is precisely the state the floor exists to catch
red: PrototypeMemoryTests.A_remembered_place_changes_what_the_creature_does_next — «prepared: memory of place changed nothing in 3 of 3 parties of the matrix — 20260726, 20260727, 20260728», and the same on baseline
mutants.whatThisDoesNotProve: It does not prove the per-party floor is stronger than the retired sum of ten — a mutant that silences exactly one party of three is not constructible by substitution, because which party goes silent is a property of the balance and not of a line of code. That the sum of ten is satisfied by 10/0/0 while the per-party rule is not is arithmetic, and it is argued in the check's own docstring and in evidence/333-memory-floor.json rather than measured here.

mutants.assertion: the reformulated post-combat detour check — the two guards that replaced the retired «a fifth of the ways round are strictly longer»
mutants.substitutionFrom: var seeing = Distance(creature.Position, destination, walls, bodies);
mutants.substitutionTo: var seeing = Distance(creature.Position, destination, walls, bodies: null);
mutants.whatItBites: the second search's knowledge of bodies, which is the only thing that makes the detour share mean anything. This is the substitution the check's own docstring promises is run here.
red: PrototypePostCombatDispersalTests.A_refused_step_after_a_fight_usually_had_a_way_round_it — «Not one of the 104 refused steps after a fight was one from which no route to the destination existed at all with bodies as walls»
mutants.note: Both new guards go to zero under it, as designed: walledIn = 0 because a search that ignores bodies always finds a route on a connected map, and longerWayRound = 0 because two searches that ignore bodies return the same length by construction.

mutants.whatItBites: no raider label is ever placed, whatever its head — the most direct denial of «every captioned returner is named unless another shares its head»
mutants.whatM10AndM10bMeasuredAboutTheOwnerScene: Neither of the first two reddens `Every_returning_raider_of_the_owners_scene_is_still_named` or `The_names_that_are_not_shown_are_raiders_sharing_one_cell`. The reason is in the checks' own docstrings and it is not a defect of the substitutions: since #76 the owner party carries at most ONE captioned returner at a time, so those two rules are exercised on a single subject and are currently satisfied by nothing being dropped. Their teeth are in the synthetic-crowd neighbours that BUILD the crowd instead of waiting for the party to produce one — `A_label_with_nowhere_to_go_is_dropped_rather_than_detached` and `A_caption_that_cannot_fit_whole_keeps_its_name_and_loses_its_sentence` — and both of those redden under M10 and M10c. What M10c shows is that the rule form still catches the thing the retired counts caught, a raider losing its name; what M10 and M10b show is that on THIS party it can only be caught by denying every raider label at once.
mutants.notOnTheList: WorldLabelInspectorTests.Every_captioned_returner_of_the_owners_frame_can_be_reached_by_clicking stays green under all three, and correctly: it is about the click target under a body, not about the label above it.

assertionsWithNoHonestMutant.assertion: «добивают труп» is absent from the simulation — No_blow_lands_on_a_raider_that_was_already_out
assertionsWithNoHonestMutant.why: It is a floor over a count that was zero before this slice and is zero after it. A substitution that makes it non-zero would have to add a mechanism that has never existed — striking a target re-read from the world as already out — rather than remove one. The check is not made worthless by that: it is a regression floor over a measured absence, and it is honest about being one.

assertionsWithNoHonestMutant.assertion: the per-party form of the memory floor is stronger than the retired sum of ten
assertionsWithNoHonestMutant.why: Which party of the three goes silent is a property of the balance, not of any single line, so no substitution produces a 10/0/0 distribution on demand. See M8.
